claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr forms a disordered BCC solid solution in the initial state.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state has substantial chemical short-range-order fluctuations.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state has severe local lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Annealing or thermal treatment promotes formation of HfTi and TiZr B2-like ordered clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr B2-like clusters form a percolating network within the BCC matrix.
B2-like ordering reduces local atomic displacement amplitudes and atomic-size-mismatch strain relative to the random matrix.
Mass and atomic-size fluctuations strongly scatter high-frequency phonons in random high-entropy alloys.
B2-like ordering homogenizes the local chemical environment and reduces variance in local interatomic potentials.
Reduced static disorder lowers the high-frequency phonon scattering rate and increases phonon lifetime.
A percolated network of ordered clusters provides continuous low-scattering pathways for phonon transport.
The transport enhancement from ordered pathways can override phonon scattering introduced by the clusters and their interfaces.
Transition from a random BCC state to a percolated B2-plus-SRO state increases lattice thermal conductivity by 10–30%.
Ordering produces high-frequency phonon modes with higher group velocities.
Ordering narrows high-frequency phonon linewidths for modes associated with B2-like clusters.
Below the cluster percolation threshold, isolated ordered clusters decrease conductivity by acting as scattering centers.
At very high temperatures, anharmonic phonon-phonon scattering masks the conductivity benefit from reduced static disorder.
The proposed conductivity increase requires coherent cluster-matrix interfaces.
The ordered clusters must remain smaller than the phonon mean free path to avoid dominant boundary scattering.
The relevant B2-ordering and SRO-percolation regime in HfNbTaTiZr is likely approximately 1000–1500 K, with room-temperature retention possible through kinetic trapping.
The fully random BCC HfNbTaTiZr baseline has low thermal conductivity because of chemical disorder and severe lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having high SRO fluctuations, while the baseline is described as fully random. If these refer to the same comparison state, substantial SRO and full chemical randomness are inconsistent.
